label: Edward J. Ruppelt
narrative: Captain Edward Ruppelt ran Project Blue Book from March 1952 to August 1953 and is the only insider of the early era who wrote it down. He inherited Project GRUDGE at its most degraded, professionalised the reporting chain, coined the term 'unidentified flying object' to replace 'flying saucer,' and presided over the July 1952 Washington sightings and the January 1953 Robertson Panel — both of which he attended in an official capacity. His 1956 book, 'The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects,' is the origin of public knowledge about the 1948 Estimate of the Situation, about the Air Force's internal split between believers and debunkers, and about the Robertson Panel's function. He was not a crank: he was the serving officer in charge, describing the machinery from inside it. The Condon Report, working under Air Force contract twelve years later, corroborated his account of the Estimate and its destruction. Ruppelt added three sceptical chapters to a 1960 edition shortly before dying of a heart attack at 37, a reversal that is variously read as genuine disillusionment or as pressure; the board records both readings and resolves neither.
